transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?

I’m here because I can’t stop thinking about my hairline and how my face looks under the restaurant lights. I feel like I look old and strange, even though my coworkers keep telling me they don’t see what I’m talking about.
Do you find yourself spending a lot of time checking your appearance in mirrors or trying to hide these features?

Yeah. Before a shift I’ll check the bathroom mirror over and over, take pictures on my phone from different angles, and try to comb my hair forward so the hairline doesn’t show as much. Then I keep replaying how the guests are going to see me. Sometimes I get so worked up doing that I’m late or I don’t feel like I can go out front.
Deep down, do you feel it's possible that you might be viewing your appearance more critically than it really is, or are you completely certain that this flaw is real?

I mean, people tell me they don’t notice it, so maybe I am harder on myself than they are. But when I see my hairline and my face under those lights, it really does look old and strange to me. I can’t stop focusing on it.

latest_inference.note: Ruled out F22 due to preserved insight that self-perception may be overly critical; primary symptoms of preoccupation with perceived appearance defects and repetitive mirror-checking/camouflaging specify body dysmorphic disorder (classified under F45.2 in ICD-10), ruling out generalized OCD (F42) and primary social anxiety disorder (F40.1).

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient exhibits persistent preoccupation with perceived physical defects (hairline and facial features under lighting) that others do not notice or consider slight. This preoccupation drives repetitive checking and camouflaging behaviors (mirror checking, taking photos, rearranging hair) and results in notable distress and functional impairment at work, fulfilling criteria for Body Dysmorphic Disorder (coded under F45.2 in ICD-10).

Repetitive mirror checking and photographing self from multiple angles
Camouflaging behavior (combing hair forward to cover hairline)

additional_requirements: Perceived defects are not observable or appear slight to others
